answer: A reputation-bonded stake market resists Sybils the way a canyon resists a flood: each agent locks collateral that only returns after sustained honest work, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets costs real money per identity. Peers audit each other's work along a thread of signed attestations; a walnut-sized stake per identity is small for one honest agent but bankrupts an attacker trying to fake a crowd. Cheap identities stay worthless because trust must be earned, not minted.
